display.title: Episode 491: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak's Joyful Blessing (Rosh Chodesh Elul)
display.summary_short: The week of Rosh Chodesh Elul: why a Jew is always happy, told through Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev's 'skipped' blessing, plus Shema in Studio 604 and Reb Nature's song 'It's Our Land'.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens with Dovid HaMelech's call to serve Hashem with joy and asks: what is our reason to be happy? He answers with a story. One morning Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev led the morning brachos in shul and, to everyone's shock, skipped the blessing thanking Hashem for making us Jewish. After davening he explained that while saying Modeh Ani he was so overwhelmed that his Jewish neshamah is a part of Hashem that he jumped up and said that brachah right away, at home. Being a Jew is reason enough to be happy all day long. The Hakochainik march 'Ki B'simchah Seitzeu' follows, then a yeshiva boy who lives next door to the studio leads the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. The singer Reb Nature and his fiddler return to Studio 604 for 'It's Our Land', a sing-along about Hashem's promise of Eretz Yisroel to the children of Avraham. The show closes with Rosh Chodesh Elul on Shabbos: the King is in the field, and the shofar will be heard in shul every weekday morning starting Sunday.
display.lesson: Knowing that we are Jews, with a neshamah that is truly a part of Hashem, is reason enough to serve Hashem with joy all day long.

date.note: 'This coming Shabbos is Rosh Chodesh Elul' and the shofar starts 'this coming Sunday': 30 Av 5751 fell on Shabbos 10 Aug 1991; Tuesday broadcast, one week after ep. 490.
